questiontext.text:
Consider the matrix \(A\) and the column vector \(\mathbf{x}\):

\[ A = {@MM@} \qquad \mathbf{x} = {@vv@} \]

Compute the matrix–vector product \(A\mathbf{x}\), if it is defined. If the product is not defined, enter the zero vector to indicate this.

(The answer box has the same number of rows as \(A\).)

\( A\mathbf{x} = \) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

[[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution:

[[ if test="is(ddef=1)" ]]

The product is defined: \(A\) is \({@m@}\times{@n@}\) and \(\mathbf{x}\) is \({@n@}\times 1\). Because the number of columns of \(A\) equals the number of entries of \(\mathbf{x}\) (\({@n@} = {@n@}\)), the product \(A\mathbf{x}\) is a \({@m@}\times 1\) column vector.

Multiply each row of \(A\) by the column \(\mathbf{x}\) by multiplying entries in matching positions and adding:

\[ A\mathbf{x} = {@MM@}\,{@vv@} = {@prod_tex@} = \boxed{{@ta@}}. \] [[/ if ]][[ if test="is(ddef=0)" ]]

The product is not defined.

\(A\) is \({@m@}\times{@n@}\), so it has \({@n@}\) columns, while \(\mathbf{x}\) has \({@p@}\) entries (it is \({@p@}\times 1\)).

For \(A\mathbf{x}\) to be defined, the number of columns of \(A\) must equal the number of entries of \(\mathbf{x}\). Since \({@n@} \neq {@p@}\), the product cannot be formed, so we enter the \({@m@}\times 1\) zero vector: \(\boxed{{@ta@}}\).

[[/ if ]]
